transcript: Header: 2027-11-16 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Daniel (Orion ML), Aisha (Orion Platform), Mark (Orion CTO)
Summary: Quick review of this week's benchmark results; decide model to pin during pilot; clarify rollback/fallback policy; next steps for latency/throughput tests.
Topics: model selection, pinning, catalog comparison, rollbacks/fallbacks, security implications for Private deployment
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll do a quick run-through of the numbers Daniel shared, then talk pinning strategy and fallback rules. Priya will cover the console steps.
[00:12] Daniel: Cool, thanks. I uploaded the spreadsheet to the shared drive — sorry, I named it orion_poc_bench_v3, it's in the folder Aisha pointed out.
[00:20] Aisha: Yep saw it, thanks. Quick note — we're particularly sensitive to 95th percentile latency for our checkout flow, target under 180 ms if possible.

[00:30] Priya: Got it. Quick context: we ran tests against four candidate models — Redwood-v2-13B-q4, Llama-3-70b-raw, Llama-2-13b-quant, and the smaller rw-chat-7b — with and without KV caching enabled. We'll compare latency, cost, and output quality on the canonical prompts.

[00:48] Mark: I want to underscore cost is important but if the smaller model causes quality regressions on NLU for returns detection we'll need to fallback rather than degrade accuracy; business impact there is high.

[01:05] Daniel: On the spreadsheet, you'll see columns for p50, p95, p99 and token cost. For p95, Redwood-v2-13B-q4 is at ~210ms on our staging (with caching), Llama-3-70b is around 310ms, rw-chat-7b is 140ms but we saw hallucinations on responsibility prompts.

[01:30] Sofia: Ok so the tradeoff is clearer — 7b meets latency but fails some correctness checks; 13B quant hits cost sweet spot but slightly above p95 target. Priya, can you remind us about fallback behavior and pinning semantics in the console?

[01:46] Priya: Yeah — pinning in Redwood means you bind a route to a specific model version, so no automatic roll to newer weights. For fallbacks we can configure a tiered policy: primary model, then a warmed fallback (e.g., a quantized variant) and a cold fallback to hosted smaller model. When warmed fallback is used we keep KV cache compatibility in mind — cross-model cache isn't safe between different architectures so we'll only warm the fallback with synthetic traffic during deploys.
[02:10] Aisha: That cache note is important — we can't afford cache misses translating to latency spikes during Black Friday-ish loads.

[02:18] Daniel: One quick transcription note — the spreadsheet labels the Redwood model 'rw-v2-13q' in places, that's me shorthand, actual model id in console is redwood-v2.1-13b-q4. Sorry for the inconsistency.

[02:30] Priya: No worries. For safety we recommend pinning to redwood-v2.1-13b-q4@2027-11-01 (example version) rather than a floating tag. That way rollouts don't surprise you. If you want more conservative behavior we can set automatic fallback thresholds: e.g., if p95 latency > 250ms or error rate > 0.5% switch to fallback for X minutes, then retry primary.
[02:55] Mark: Are fallbacks seamless for sessions? We use session-based conversations in checkout support, so losing context would be terrible.

[03:03] Priya: Good question — we use KV cache to preserve past tokens for a route, but as I said, switching across model families may not preserve binary cache. We recommend pinning primary and pre-warming fallback with a short prefix of recent sessions for critical routes; otherwise we accept a cold-start context window of ~1-2 tokens which can be mitigated by explicit context rehydration in your app.
[03:25] Daniel: For our pilot we can tolerate a small context redaction during failover if it reduces latency and errors temporarily, but prefer warmed fallback for checkout support.
[03:33] Sofia: Sounds reasonable. Let's talk catalog comparisons — Priya, you had notes on model quality differences?

[03:38] Priya: Right — qualitative evals: Redwood-v2.1-13b-q4 performed best on our returns detection and extraction prompts, Llama-3-70b had higher factuality but cost and latency are worse, rw-chat-7b was decent for short chit-chat but failed on edge-case prompts. Quantized Llama-2-13b was close to redwood-v2 for cost but slightly worse on hallucination metrics.
[04:02] Aisha: So recommendation would be pin to redwood-v2.1-13b-q4 for checkout route, with warmed fallback to Llama-2-13b-quant and cold fallback to rw-chat-7b? Does that ordering make sense?

[04:14] Priya: The warmed fallback should ideally be another redwood family variant like redwood-v2.1-13b-q3 or a quantized version with compatible KV layout; Llama variants may not share cache semantics. If we use Llama as fallback we commit to rehydration steps.
[04:32] Mark: Ok so from a platform POV, pre-warming a compatible quantized variant is preferable even if cost is slightly higher.
[04:40] Daniel: I can add a column to the benchmark sheet marking cache-compatibility and recommended warm/cold tags.

[04:48] Sofia: Great — then action is pin checkout route to redwood-v2.1-13b-q4@2027-11-01 and configure warmed fallback to redwood-v2.1-13b-q3@2027-10-20 (example). Priya, can you outline the rollback steps if the pinned model causes regressions?

[05:05] Priya: Yep — rollback is manual via the Console or API. Steps: 1) switch route to previously pinned version (we keep a version history), 2) trigger synthetic traffic to verify, 3) if needed escalate to Redwood support for emergency rollback which can be faster if you allow it in the POc contract. We'll send screenshots. Also recommend a canary window (5-10%) for the first hour before full rollout.
[05:30] Aisha: Is there audit logging for these changes? We need SSO+RBAC compliance so only certain roles can change pins.
[05:36] Priya: Yes, Console logs who made the change, timestamps, and we can integrate with your SIEM via webhook. We also support SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC for routes.

[05:45] Mark: Ok good. Another question: if we pin a model in Dedicated or Private, are kernel selections and quantization deterministic so performance matches hosted numbers? We want reproducible results.

[05:56] Priya: There can be slight variations due to hardware and kernel paths. For Dedicated we can match the cluster config we used in benchmark; for Private on-prem you need the same GPU family and driver stack. We'll provide a compatibility checklist; customer-managed KMS/HSM is supported for Private.
[06:15] Daniel: Back to latency — the spreadsheet shows p95 at 210ms for redwood-v2-13b-q4 with KV caching. If we pre-warm the fallback as you suggested, what p95 do you expect for warm fallback?

[06:25] Priya: Warm fallback will be close to primary, maybe +10-30ms. Cold fallback to rw-chat-7b is lower latency but less accurate. Important: warmed fallback must be same family or quantization scheme to reuse KV entries.

[06:37] Sofia: Let's settle on a concrete plan for the pilot: pin checkout route to redwood-v2.1-13b-q4@2027-11-01, warm fallback to redwood-v2.1-13b-q3, set canary to 10% for 1 hour, automatic fallback trigger if p95 > 250ms for 5 consecutive minutes, and manual rollback procedure documented. Does everyone agree?
[06:58] Aisha: Agree, with the note that we need the RBAC audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[07:05] Mark: Agree as well. Also include a cost cap alert — if spend per route increases 30% we want a slack alert and auto-switch to cheaper fallback.
[07:15] Priya: We can set usage alerts and cost thresholds; we'll add that to the runbook we'll share.
[07:21] Daniel: Quick nit — in the sheet I have the 'warm' column but it's blank for Llama models. I'll update to mark only redwood-compatible variants as warmable.
[07:30] Sofia: Perfect. Any outstanding technical risks? Daniel or Aisha?
[07:36] Daniel: Only caveat is our staging env is smaller than production, so absolute p95 may increase. We'll run a scaled run next week per action item.
[07:43] Aisha: From platform side we need the pre-warm orchestration steps documented to coordinate traffic mirroring, otherwise we risk cache-mismatch.
[07:50] Priya: We'll send a step-by-step pre-warm playbook including the API calls to warm KV cache and sample synthetic traffic generator commands.

[07:58] Sofia: Ok let's recap: Sofia will send updated benchmark with highlighted pinned rows and cost/latency tradeoffs; Priya sends pinning/rollback/fallback docs and console screenshots; Daniel runs scaled latency tests and marks cache-compatibility columns; next sync in one week same time unless the team wants an ad-hoc call after the scaled run. Any other items?
[08:18] Mark: Can you also include a short note on encryption options for Private? We need to review KMS options.
[08:24] Priya: Will include KMS/HSM notes and link to compliance pack.
[08:28] Sofia: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email and Slack with the links. Meeting end.
Notes: minor transcription artifacts — product names abbreviated in the sheet. Speaker labels approximate; some timestamps are coarse.
